correctness.rationale: Cubic closed neighborhoods exclude three dominators. If a four-set dominates, the point and line coverage inequalities force two of each. For chosen points p,q the selected lines must avoid them and cover all five other points. Their intersection must be the third point r of pq: at any other candidate intersection there are two distinct lines to p and q and only one line left. Conversely the two lines through r other than pq cover the five required points and are exactly the two lines not incident to p or q. This yields 21 concepts. Every vertex has frequency six. Pair frequencies are one for same-type pairs by point-pair uniqueness and duality, three for nonincidence by choosing r on the line, and zero for incidence. Hence all four traces occur exactly on nonedges (counts t,6−t,6−t,9+t), and any triple contains a same-type pair with just one all-positive witness, forbidding one of its two third-vertex extensions. Complement connectivity follows from the two part-cliques and cross nonedges. Contracting a spanning tree leaves 70−14+1=57 loops, proving the homotopy statement. For the online lower bound use point 1 and functional 1 as the first two queries in the binary labeling. The line contains points 2,4,6; the concepts containing it have point pairs among {1,3,5,7}. The third queries at points 2,3,2,3 have respective positive counts 5,2,1,1 among 12,3,3,3 surviving concepts, as also checked by an independent exhaustive witness replay. A root positive branch always has just six concepts and cannot realize eight leaves, giving the upper bound. The topology is that of a one-dimensional graph, not the clique complex of its 1-skeleton.
residual_risks: No inference is made about all inclusion-minimal sets, all maximal independent sets, or higher-order planes. Replay confirms the finite online witness; the written trace and coverage arguments independently establish the other conclusions.

value.rationale: This is the natural ordinary minimum-domination class of the smallest projective-plane incidence graph. The complete Boolean traces recover exactly the nonincidence/nonadjacency relation, and the explicit small adaptive tree provides a robust witness that even this symmetric set class distinguishes online and fixed-query shattering. The obstruction and tree are useful independent of the known optimal size; the cycle rank quantifies the geometry of the resulting support complex. Value does not rest on a routine 21-set census.
residual_risks: Motivated single finite example, not a uniform theorem for incidence graphs or a new general learning bound.
